status: Held-out fixture for the ADR 0017 step 2 matcher gate. Built from the cycle 2 capture alone, so the S1, S2, and S3 prohibitions are matched against a document whose wording never saw them.

authoredFrom.note: Entries are the step 1 entries whose concern is reached by at least one cycle 2 grammar-reject prohibition, carried over unchanged in wording and ruled active. Nothing was rewritten for this condition.

entries.concern: Real personal or health information in frame
entries.statement: Do not show real names, dates of birth, diagnoses, phone numbers, account details, clinical results, or message histories on any screen or paper surface. Visible content is invented.

basis.derivedFrom: The Official Website states privacy is paramount and describes the platform as HIPAA compliant. Reached by four grammar-reject captures and one regenerated guardrail. No approved guardrail states this rule.

entries.concern: Identity artwork rebuilt from a screenshot
entries.statement: Do not redraw, approximate, stretch, crop, recolor, or reconstruct the Dialog Health logo or its approved arrangements. Place the supplied artwork unaltered, and use RCS Template.png unchanged in its role.

basis.derivedFrom: Approved guardrail against reconstructing exact identity assets, naming the brand kit as the authority for logos and lockups and RCS Template.png as a separate canonical background asset. Reached by four grammar-reject captures and three regenerated guardrails.

entries.concern: The platform staged as clinical treatment
entries.statement: Do not arrange the product as medication, diagnostic equipment, dosage instructions, or a treatment tool. It stays visibly in the communication and workflow role.

basis.derivedFrom: The Official Website positions Dialog Health as healthcare communication software rather than a clinical treatment. Reached by one grammar-reject capture.

entries.concern: Unreal technology imagery instead of a real scene
entries.statement: Do not use floating message bubbles, artificial interface overlays, glowing data trails, or decorative message streams in place of a real phone, a real room, and a person acting.

basis.derivedFrom: Approved lived-world reject of generic technology spectacle disconnected from healthcare work. Reached by one grammar-reject capture.

entries.concern: Demonstration material presented as identity or fact
entries.statement: Do not present the fictional sender name, sample logos, invented screens, patient names, dates, or message designs from the RCS deck as Dialog Health identity assets or as a live customer deployment.

basis.derivedFrom: Approved guardrail keeping sales examples in their proper role: the RCS presentation is representative sales evidence that can be improved, and its WynterHealth examples are demonstrations. Reached by two grammar-reject captures and three regenerated guardrails.
